video_title: Bringing Back Skin in the Game ft. ARES
gist: Morgan Lie, founder of Aries Pro (title spells it ARES), argues memecoins and prediction markets are information-native assets whose traders face a discovery problem that execution-focused apps like Robinhood and Coinbase ignore. Aries is a social, mobile-first prediction-market aggregator where every post is tied to a real trade; copy trading already drives over 50% of its volume, and the long-term goal is a data and AI moat that explains why odds move.

insights.claim: Morgan Lie argues memecoins and prediction-market contracts are the first assets with no financial value and no store-of-value role: they have expiration dates and pure information value, so trading them is effectively trading information.
insights.speaker: Morgan Lie (Aries Pro)
insights.so_what: Value drivers for these assets are attention and narrative, so edge comes from information flow rather than fundamentals.
insights.quote: both Minkcoin and prediction market are the first assets that actually they they don't have like financial values

insights.claim: Prior-generation trading platforms like Robinhood and Coinbase are built for execution by traders who already know what they want; narrative-driven assets create a discovery problem that the next generation of financial apps must solve.
insights.speaker: Morgan Lie (Aries Pro)
insights.so_what: Watch for incumbents adding discovery/social layers; whoever owns pre-trade attention may disintermediate execution venues.
insights.quote: they were all very much focusing on execution right they serve as a destination for traders who already know what they want to buy and sell

insights.claim: Morgan Lie's early pump.fun investment (early 2024) was a bet on unusual early volume and engagement frequency despite an esoteric asset and a janky website, and it revealed a 'prosumer trading' trend of hundreds of thousands to millions of users trenching memecoins 6-12 hours a day.
insights.speaker: Morgan Lie (Aries Pro)
insights.so_what: Engagement frequency and volume can be the leading signal for new trading categories before the category is legible.

insights.claim: Memecoin trading is unintuitive for consumers because buying Dogecoin is really a bet on how long attention lasts, whereas prediction markets are simple binary bets constrained by time and choices.
insights.speaker: Morgan Lie (Aries Pro)
insights.so_what: Supports prediction markets gaining consumer share relative to memecoins as the vehicle for narrative speculation.

insights.claim: New narrative-asset mechanisms such as noise.xyz (reportedly Paradigm-backed) and Trendle let users go long or short on trends that memecoins used to represent, using a binary-like mechanism.
insights.speaker: Morgan Lie (Aries Pro)
insights.so_what: Early-stage experiments in tradable trends/attention; potential new venues or tokens to monitor.

insights.claim: Morgan Lie expects information-native trading mechanisms to move in seasons and cycles like memecoins, with mechanisms working for a while and then being replaced, making it hard to predict which will stick.
insights.speaker: Morgan Lie (Aries Pro)
insights.so_what: Favor aggregators/platform layers over betting on a single mechanism or venue.

insights.claim: Memecoin volumes are down from the boom though the segment still exists.
insights.speaker: host
insights.so_what: Memecoin-dependent businesses face cyclical volume risk.

insights.claim: Narrative is increasingly driving equities too: Morgan Lie says Tesla's price tomorrow depends more on how people feel about Elon Musk's tweets than on fundamentals, and the host cites Sweetgreen pushing a viral wrap despite worse margins to shift investor perception.
insights.speaker: Morgan Lie (Aries Pro)
insights.so_what: Sentiment/attention data becomes a tradable input for narrative-sensitive equities, not just crypto.
insights.quote: Tesla's price tomorrow depends so much on how people feel about what Elon Musk is tweaking today

insights.claim: Polymarket and Kalshi dominate prediction markets, with Kalshi leading in the US due to regulatory advantage, but that moat is eroding as licensed institutions like Gemini launch their own prediction markets.
insights.speaker: Morgan Lie (Aries Pro)
insights.so_what: Kalshi's US regulatory moat may compress as licensed exchanges enter; expect fragmentation and fee competition.
insights.quote: a lot of people didn't know that Germani launched their own needed prediction market end of last year

insights.claim: Builders are using primitives such as Hyperliquid to construct their own prediction markets, which Morgan Lie is very bullish on as a driver of market-creation breadth.
insights.speaker: Morgan Lie (Aries Pro)
insights.so_what: Hyperliquid infrastructure may capture prediction-market activity; watch HIP-style market creation.

insights.claim: Current prediction-market offerings are narrow (US politics, crypto, US-centric sports), yet the majority of Polymarket's volume comes from outside the US, leaving underserved European and LatAm markets.
insights.speaker: Morgan Lie (Aries Pro)
insights.so_what: Localized non-US event markets are a growth vector; infrastructure that lowers market-creation cost could drive exponential growth.
insights.quote: mass majority of poly markets volume is actually outside United States because of regulatory kind like constraint

insights.claim: Morgan Lie's survey work shows two Polymarket user types: those who trade and a growing number who use it as a source of truth to find news.
insights.speaker: Morgan Lie (Aries Pro)
insights.so_what: Prediction-market data is becoming a media/news product, opening data-licensing and content monetization.

insights.claim: Many prediction-market traders are optimizing for entertainment, intellectual exploration and bragging rights with friends rather than purely profit, unlike equity or crypto traders.
insights.speaker: Morgan Lie (Aries Pro)
insights.so_what: Product and monetization for this segment should be modeled like entertainment/social, not pure brokerage.

themes.theme: Aries Pro: social attention layer before execution

insights.claim: Aries Pro is building a mobile-first, social-media-first trading app that prompts users to post commentary on every trade, creating an 'attention layer before execution' to drive daily engagement.
insights.speaker: Morgan Lie (Aries Pro)
insights.so_what: A social-first front end could own user acquisition and routing for prediction markets and later other assets.
insights.quote: we are essentially building a attention layer before execution

insights.claim: Aries aims to be a Twitter alternative where every post is tied to an actual trade, ranking content by conviction and historical win rate to reduce noise, because on Twitter it costs nothing to say anything.
insights.speaker: Morgan Lie (Aries Pro)
insights.so_what: Skin-in-the-game ranked content could become a higher-signal sentiment source than social media.
insights.quote: The current problem with social media especially at Twitter is it costs nothing to say anything

insights.claim: Aries aggregates Polymarket, Kalshi and Limitless and aims to provide best-price order routing across venues, since users care about price and liquidity rather than which venue lists a market.
insights.speaker: Morgan Lie (Aries Pro)
insights.so_what: Aggregation commoditizes individual venues; liquidity and pricing become the venue battleground.

insights.claim: More than 63% of Aries traders engage with copy trading, copy trading drives over 50% of platform volume, and the trader leaderboard analytics page gets the most time spent.
insights.speaker: Morgan Lie (Aries Pro)
insights.so_what: Copy trading is the core engagement and volume engine for consumer prediction-market apps.
insights.quote: more more than 63% of our trader engage with our copy trading feature

insights.claim: Because event-driven markets lack fundamentals to analyze, users constantly look for insights from other humans, which explains the demand for leaderboards and copy trading.
insights.speaker: Morgan Lie (Aries Pro)
insights.so_what: Social-signal and trader-reputation products have structural demand in event markets.
insights.quote: there's no fundamentals for you to do fundamental analysis. So people are constantly trying to find insights from other humans

insights.claim: Aries prioritizes retention above all because roughly 80% of fintech trading users lose money and churn within about a month, followed by time-to-first-deposit and first trade.
insights.speaker: Morgan Lie (Aries Pro)
insights.so_what: Content that gives value independent of P&L is the retention hedge for trading apps; evaluate peers on retention, not just signups.

insights.claim: Aries plans to expand beyond prediction markets to other asset classes, calling inclusion of other assets a no-brainer once the attention-first experience works.
insights.speaker: Morgan Lie (Aries Pro)
insights.so_what: Potential competitor to eToro/Robinhood-style multi-asset social brokerages over time.

insights.claim: eToro, a public company focused mainly on Europe, already combines social feeds with copy trading; Morgan Lie says over 1 million of its roughly 3 million+ users engage with copy trading.
insights.speaker: Morgan Lie (Aries Pro)
insights.so_what: Validates copy trading as a scaled business model that prediction-market apps can port.

insights.claim: A top trader copied on eToro reportedly manages about $250 million and earns about 1% management fee, roughly $2.5 million a year, from others copying his trades.
insights.speaker: Morgan Lie (Aries Pro)
insights.so_what: Shows monetizable demand for retail-trader-as-fund-manager, a template for prediction-market copy trading.

insights.claim: On copy-trading platforms historical track record matters most; content creation helps attract followers but a good content creator who is a bad trader will not be copied.
insights.speaker: Morgan Lie (Aries Pro)
insights.so_what: Performance-verified reputation beats follower counts, unlike Twitter.

insights.claim: Prediction-market copy trading needs a different design than eToro's financial-summary feed because the content is faster, more conversational and more entertaining.
insights.speaker: Morgan Lie (Aries Pro)
insights.so_what: Room for a new entrant rather than eToro to own social prediction-market trading.

insights.claim: The host notes convergence between fintech and social: trading apps like eToro integrate social feeds while Twitter adds features (described as hashtags).
insights.speaker: host
insights.so_what: Expect competition between social platforms and brokerages for the pre-trade attention layer.

themes.theme: Data moat: explaining why odds move

insights.claim: Polymarket predicts outcomes precisely but does not explain why odds shift; Aries aims to capture which narratives traders on each side engage with, so it can explain real-time odds moves.
insights.speaker: Morgan Lie (Aries Pro)
insights.so_what: Causal-attribution data on odds moves could be sold to campaigns, corporates and funds.
insights.quote: the data on poly market doesn't really tell us why why the odds is trending or shifting to certain direction at any given time

insights.claim: Morgan Lie gives the example that a campaign manager could use Aries data to see that bettors against a candidate all engaged with a specific negative narrative and use it for crisis management.
insights.speaker: Morgan Lie (Aries Pro)
insights.so_what: Illustrates an enterprise/political data product beyond retail trading revenue.

insights.claim: Morgan Lie claims trade-linked narrative data is the highest-leverage data no internet company currently has, and plans to train a proprietary AI model to become best-in-class at predicting the future.
insights.speaker: Morgan Lie (Aries Pro)
insights.so_what: If realized, Aries becomes a data/AI company with a forecasting-model moat rather than a pure trading front end.
insights.quote: this is the highest leverage data that internet no internet company has right now

insights.claim: Morgan Lie chose crypto over AI in 2022-23 because AI is about optimization that gives exponential advantage to whoever has resources, whereas permissionless tech enables redistribution of power and liquidity to individuals over the next 10-20 years.
insights.speaker: Morgan Lie (Aries Pro)
insights.so_what: Frames crypto's value proposition as decentralizing counterweight to AI-driven concentration.
insights.quote: the nature of AI I is very much about optimization

insights.claim: Morgan Lie says crypto has spent about 20 years building infrastructure and the key problem now is adoption; even crypto founders use Venmo instead of stablecoins to split bills, so new builders should abstract crypto away from users.
insights.speaker: Morgan Lie (Aries Pro)
insights.so_what: Value accrues to consumer apps that hide crypto rails; ideology-led infra plays face an adoption gap.
insights.quote: I'm a crypto founder but I still use VMO why am I not [laughter] sending stable coin

insights.claim: Morgan Lie argues people with prediction-market edge need not be financially sophisticated but lack capital, and copy trading can connect them with capital holders to create a new path to wealth.
insights.speaker: Morgan Lie (Aries Pro)
insights.so_what: Opens a retail 'emerging manager' market and associated fee revenue.
